title: The Marriage Ceremony (A Play)
subject: English Language
objectives: Read and understand a dramatic play
Learn how traditional Nigerian marriage ceremonies are conducted

blocks.caption: A traditional marriage ceremony in Nigeria.

blocks.md: This is a play about a traditional Nigerian marriage ceremony. The class should dramatise it. Read the characters' lines out loud and imagine the scene.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mr. Adebayo's compound, one Friday evening. Mr. and Mrs. Adebayo and their family members are seated on one side. They are led by Chief Adefemi, Mr. Adebayo's eldest brother. The groom and his parents' family members are seated on the other side. The ceremony is about to begin.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: Good afternoon to all.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Good afternoon. You are welcome.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: We have knocked before we entered this house.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: You have entered, welcome.

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: Our son found a flower in your compound and we wish to pluck it.

lines.speaker: Chief Adefemi
lines.text: Which flower? In this compound?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: Yes. My father, Chief Adeloye, told me to plead with you all to let us pluck it.

lines.speaker: Chief Adefemi
lines.text: There are many flowers in this compound. Doesn't the one you found have a name? Hibiscus, frangipani, tetanus? What?

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: (All laugh.)

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: It has a name, my father. All of us, as well dressed as we are, have come to pick one flower, just one. We have come with goats and chickens, yams and fruits, honey and money. Loads of money. Because the flower is a person.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: A flower is now a person! (All laugh.)

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: Yes. She is Adunola. Your beautiful Adunola, the sweet Adunola, who is sweeter than the honey we have brought here. She is the flower!

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: Is that so? And who had the sharp eyes to see a flower so hidden in our compound?

lines.speaker: Mrs. Orelope
lines.text: It was our son, Rotimi, who knows the best place to search.

lines.speaker: Chief Adefemi
lines.text: Bring him in. Let us see how sharp he can see.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rotimi and his friends enter led by Mrs. Orelope as music is playing and all are dancing. Then he prostrates before Mr. Adebayo's family members to greet them. Adunola is led in by her friends and other wives of their family members. She kneels before her parents.

lines.speaker: Chief Adefemi
lines.text: Rotimi, you may rise. They say you are sharp-eyed and have seen a flower in this house. Right? Find out for yourself. Is this the flower?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rotimi is allowed to unveil Adunola.

lines.speaker: Rotimi
lines.text: Yes, father.

lines.speaker: All
lines.text: (All clap and shout in joy.)

blocks.md: **About the Play:** In many Nigerian cultures, marriage ceremonies involve the groom's family formally asking for the bride's hand. The 'flower' is a poetic way of describing the bride. The whole ceremony is full of tradition, respect, and celebration.

quiz.q: What does the 'flower' stand for in the play?
quiz.explain: The 'flower' is the beautiful bride, Adunola.

quiz.q: Who is the father of the bride?
quiz.explain: Adunola is the daughter of Mr. Adebayo.

quiz.q: What did the groom's family bring as gifts?
options: Goats, chickens, yams, fruits, honey, and money
quiz.explain: They brought goats, chickens, yams, fruits, honey, and loads of money.

quiz.q: What is the name of the groom?
What happens when Rotimi unveils Adunola?
options: Everyone claps and shouts in joy
quiz.explain: Everyone claps and shouts in joy to confirm the marriage.
